findings.location: crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_nav_icon_rail.rs:784 assert_rail_offers (every narrow-rail row routes through it), with the per-member iconLaidOut already read at crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/rail_reading.rs:137
findings.obligation: S2 scope-in obligation 1: 'The collapsed left nav shows an icon for every destination the expanded nav shows the operator, and an icon for Sign out.' Also the S2 stimulus/expected pair, which says she reaches her destinations 'by activating their icons in the narrow rail'.
findings.observation: BLOCKING. Nothing in the lane ever asserts that a narrow-rail member DRAWS its icon. assert_rail_offers observes the accessible name, inLayout, visible and focusable; iconPresent/iconLaidOut are collected for every member by the shared probe and are used in exactly one place - given_rights_with_the_nav_open:122, the NEGATIVE assertion that the OPEN nav draws none. So the positive half of the slice's first obligation has no falsifier. A narrow rail of empty targets - each member a one-pixel-wide clipped word, no glyph at all - satisfies every assertion in the lane: the accessible name still computes from the clipped text (which is the design's own name mechanism, architecture.md:26), visible() is true because the probe's threshold is rect.width >= 1 && rect.height >= 1, and focusable() is true. The design names this exact wrong outcome as a risk at architecture.md:2150 ('an item whose word is clipped AND whose icon is absent, which looks like an empty target'), and the acceptance row's admitted limit covers only the WRONG picture, never the ABSENT one. Combined with the next finding this is a fully green oracle over a strip the operator sees as blank slivers.
findings.remediation: In the narrow-rail reading, assert that every member reports iconLaidOut true and that its icon box has a real size on screen (a pressable target, not a sub-pixel sliver) - both facts are already in the reading, so this is one assertion inside assert_rail_offers guarded by the narrow state, with a WHAT/WHY/HOW message naming the members that draw nothing. Do not assert which glyph is drawn: that limit stays admitted as written.

findings.obligation: P3's visible half - 'a pointer operator sees it' / E4 - and the S2 declared falsifier 'the focused icon shows no visible label'. Feature row: 'each icon she stops on shows the name of the place it opens, in a box she can see'.
findings.observation: BLOCKING, vacuous under the design's own mechanism. labelShown is labelRect.width >= 1 && labelRect.height >= 1 && no ancestor display:none/visibility:hidden/inert/hidden && no ancestor opacity < 0.05, where labelRect is label.getBoundingClientRect(). getBoundingClientRect reports the LAYOUT box: it is unaffected by clip, by clip-path, and by clipping from an ancestor's overflow. The design requires the collapsed label to stay in the document 'clipped to one pixel rather than given display:none' (architecture.md:26), so in the UNREVEALED state labelRect is 1x1 - and 1 >= 1 passes. With clip-path the layout box stays at full size and passes even more plainly. Therefore once span.sidebar__label exists, labelShown is true for every rail member whether or not the flyout ever reveals anything: a crafter whose :focus-visible flyout rule is missing, mis-selectored or never triggered gets a green scenario, and the operator still has to press a glyph to find out where it goes. The assertion cannot fail for the reason it exists; only a label of literally zero size would trip it.
findings.remediation: Make the observation a differential inside one reading, using data the shared probe already collects (members[].labelBox at rail_reading.rs:136): require the FOCUSED member's label box to be materially larger than the same label's clipped box when it does not hold the focus (or than its unfocused siblings' label boxes), and/or hit-test the label's centre with document.elementFromPoint and require the result to be the label or a descendant of it. Either observation is false for a label that is never revealed and true only for one the operator can actually see; neither needs the flyout's position or styling, which stay unobserved as declared.

findings.obligation: P6: 'no link is left focusable or announced while it is invisible', and the restated nav-collapse-toggle scenario whose stated RED-trigger is 'a destination is hidden by width, by opacity or by CLIPPING its icon away'.
findings.observation: NON-BLOCKING, incomplete falsifier for one named mechanism. visibleNow rejects display:none, visibility:hidden/collapse, inert, hidden, opacity < 0.05 and a zero-sized box - so hiding by width and hiding by opacity are both caught, as the module doc claims. Clipping is not: neither clip, clip-path nor an ancestor's overflow changes getBoundingClientRect, so a destination clipped away while it keeps its layout box reads as visible, invisibleFocusable stays empty, and the law passes. That mechanism is not hypothetical to this design - its own Quint model records init_hide_clip as a violating state (architecture.md:1146), and both feature files' RED-trigger comments advertise clipping as caught. Not blocking: the slice's plausible implementation clips the LABEL, not the member, and the two mechanisms that this slice could regress into are observed; but the claim the comments make is wider than the observation.
findings.remediation: Either extend visibleNow with a hit test (document.elementFromPoint at the member's centre resolving to the member or a descendant, which also catches a covered member), or narrow the two RED-trigger comments and the module doc to the mechanisms actually observed - width, zero size, opacity, display and visibility - so the oracle does not claim a falsifier it does not carry. The hit test is preferred: it closes the mechanism the design model names.

findings.location: docs/feature/nav-collapse-icon-rail/architecture.md:690 (the declared observable for the revealed label)
findings.obligation: The declared verification must distinguish P3's promised outcome - the operator can read where an icon goes before she presses it - from the plausible wrong behaviour the same design admits: a label clipped to one pixel and never revealed.
findings.observation: NON-BLOCKING, design-owned cause of the vacuous focused-label observation. The design fixes the observable as 'whether the label of a focused or hovered icon is visible: a box with a non-zero width that shows the destination word'. The same design fixes the unrevealed collapsed label as a box clipped to ONE PIXEL that stays in the document (architecture.md:26). A one-pixel box has a non-zero width, so the declared observable is satisfied by the very state it is meant to exclude; the oracle implemented the declared observable faithfully and inherited its blind spot. Keeping 'where the flyout sits and how it is styled' unobserved (architecture.md:696) does not require weakening the observable this far.
findings.remediation: Restate the declared observable so it separates revealed from clipped - for example 'the focused or hovered label is painted where the operator can see it: its box is materially larger than the clipped box the same label has without the focus, or its centre hit-tests to the label' - and keep the flyout's position and styling out of scope as already recorded. No mechanism changes; this is the observation sentence only.

diagnostic: REJECTED on two blocking oracle findings; everything else in the S2 oracle is sound and its judgment is retained. What is right: the lane drives the real browser against the one in-process origin through the operator's own press, keystroke, navigation and screen width; the owed destination set is derived from the rights read back out of the store, never off the page; the audible half of the naming promise is read from the browser's own accessibility tree rather than from markup; every narrow measurement is guarded by the mark plus a strip strictly narrower than the shipped 240 px; the rights-revoked comeback row, the two no-script arms and the open-nav-has-no-icon assertion are real falsifiers for the scope-out promises; the rail reading moved to support/rail_reading.rs, so no step module depends on another; and the RED is semantic, reconciling row for row with the missing production behaviour at this revision (reused from the author's run at this same clean commit, no new execution claimed). What blocks: (1) the slice's first obligation - an icon for every destination - has no falsifier at all; iconLaidOut is collected per member and used only to assert the OPEN nav draws none. (2) The 'name in a box she can see' assertion cannot fail once the label span exists, because labelShown reads getBoundingClientRect, which ignores clip, clip-path and ancestor overflow, and the design's unrevealed label is a one-pixel box that passes a >= 1 threshold. Together they let a narrow rail of blank one-pixel slivers with no glyph and no flyout be fully green, which is the dead end this feature exists to remove. Both corrections are local to the oracle, use facts the shared probe already reads, need no architecture change and add no scope. Two non-blocking findings travel with them: the member-visibility observation is blind to clip-hiding, the mechanism the design's own model names as the violation, while both feature files advertise it as caught; and the design's declared observable at architecture.md:690 is the cause of the second blocker and should be restated with it. Re-review is limited to those findings and to P1, P3 and P6.
